newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Majority of Swedes want referendum on EMU-poll.
newsitem.headline: Majority of Swedes want referendum on EMU-poll.

text.p: The majority of Swedes want a referendum on Sweden's possible participation in the European Union's currency union and would vote against such a move, a poll published on Thursday showed.

The Gallup poll, published in Swedish tabloid Expressen, found six out of 10 Swedes wanted the chance to vote on whether Sweden should join the Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) that is due to come into effect on January 1, 1999.
Twenty-six percent of the 1,000 people questioned did not want a referendum and 14 percent were uncertain.
Asked how they would vote if there was a referendum today, 54 percent of those questioned said they would say no to EMU.
Only 21 percent were in favour of joining EMU and 23 percent were uncertain.
Swedes living in the north of the country were most opposed to EMU membership, with 71 percent against Sweden pooling into Europe's single currency.
A referendum can be called in Sweden if a third of the 349 member parliament backs the move.
At present only the centre party, left, and green parties have backed a call for a referendum but these parties together only hold about 70 seats in parliament.
